Ballot Basics

Peer-shareable local ballot explainers, built from forty interviews with first-time voters.

First-time voting is a social act — information travels through trusted peers, not portals.

The problem

First-time voters can find national coverage everywhere and local ballot information almost nowhere.

The team’s first instinct was to build a portal. Forty interviews killed that idea: first-time voters don’t search — they ask someone they trust.

Ballot Basics leaned into that. Instead of a destination, the team built explainers designed to be handed from one person to another: shareable, local, and written like a friend talking.

The interview protocol that got forty strangers talking honestly is in the Learning Library, ready for the next team’s topic.

OutcomeForty first-time voters interviewed; explainers shared peer-to-peer in the pilot; the interview kit returned to the commons.
TeamElena Ruiz, Marcus Bell (Mentor), and two teammates
